transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-15
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SRE), Hannah Cho (CSM) — Amira Patel (BlueHarbor), Tom Reynolds (BlueHarbor), Sofia Kim (BlueHarbor), Daniel Wu (BlueHarbor)

Summary:
- Week 8 POC sync focused on last night's kernel upgrade fallout and runforward/rollback options; validated fallback routing behavior; agreed on concrete runbook and SOC2 evidence checkpoint; action items assigned.
- Observed 2x latency spike during one canary window when K-V caching warmed; not reproducible on staging yet.

Topics: kernel upgrade regression, canary fallback behavior, VPC egress shaping, MTU issues between on-prem and provider, SOC2 evidence & data residency, next steps for acceptance sign-off.

Action items (brief): see metadata list.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Ethan: All right, hi everyone thanks for joining. This is... Ethan Park from Redwood. We are on for 46 minutes. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Amira: Hi Amira here, BlueHarbor ML.
[00:10] Tom: Tom, infra.
[00:12] Sofia: Sofia, security.
[00:14] Daniel: Daniel platform.
[00:16] Maya: Maya from Redwood SE. Hi all.
[00:18] Luis: Luis, SRE at Redwood.
[00:20] Ethan: Cool. Agenda, we want to walk through the incident from last night's canary kernel upgrade, review the fallback routing that kicked in, confirm runbook, and then narrow acceptance criteria for the POC.

[02:05] Amira: Quick context from our side — this POC is gating our decision for Q1, we need consistent p95 under 220ms for customer facing llm endpoints and also strict egress controls for patient data.
[02:30] Ethan: Understood, p95 220ms. We mapped SLA target in the deck. Also note the private deployment with VPC peering + egress NAT we configured — that was used in the canary.

[04:12] Tom: The weird thing we saw: during the first 10 minute canary, one of the GPU nodes started seeing token latency spikes to ~1.1s for a subset of sequences. It correlated with a KV cache warm event but not exactly. The logs show repeated small spikes but then the circuit breaker tripped and traffic shifted to the hosted fallback.
[04:45] Luis: Yeah I can add — our runtime telemetry shows the kernel patch changed a memory allocation path, so for longer contexts > 1k tokens we saw sporadic GC-like stalls. That manifested as 2-3 token delays, accumulative to the observed spike.
[05:05] Maya: To be clear, this was only in the canary group, we auto-rolled back the canary but apparently some requests still landed on the canaried nodes during the rollback window. So there's a short sweet-spot where mixed routing happened.

[06:20] Sofia: From security, our main concern is whether any fallbacks sent patient PII outside the VPC control plane; the logs we saw show egress to the Redwood-hosted fallback region. We need to confirm encryption in transit and at rest for that path and whether logs/audit retained any text.
[06:50] Ethan: Good flag. Two quick things: 1) the fallback path uses TLS and the private control plane still enforces field-level redaction when configured, but we will confirm exactly which logs contained user text during that interval; 2) we will also verify KMS usage on fallback shards.

[08:01] Daniel: Also we hit an MTU mismatch between our edge router and the cloud egress which caused packet fragmentation and reassembly overhead — I wonder if that could have amplified latency. We captured pcap and traceroute.
[08:22] Luis: MTU issues can absolutely induce extra latency for certain RPC sizes — good catch. Please upload the pcap, we'll take a look.

[09:10] Tom: I uploaded a short pcap to the shared folder right after the incident.
[09:16] Ethan: Perfect thanks. We'll correlate.

[10:00] Maya: I want to propose a structured rollback/runforward plan: we keep the kernel upgrade disabled for full production; for canaries we add an extra health check that verifies KV cache hit rate consistency and memory allocation metrics before allowing traffic at 50% ramp. Also add a routing policy that pins canary users to stable pool on failure.
[10:35] Amira: Sounds reasonable. How long before full production if the canary passes? We need a timeline.
[10:45] Maya: Typically we'd run two successful 2-hour canaries across different traffic shapes, then a 24-hour soak with increased volume. For this POC we can compress to two 90-min windows with the additional health checks given your timeline.

[12:00] Sofia: For compliance: can you confirm you have SOC2 + ISO vocab? We need evidence for the private deployment specifically — where logs are stored, retention, and who has KMS access.
[12:20] Ethan: We are SOC2 Type II; we also have an ISO cert in process. We'll share the SOC2 envelope and the auditor contact. For the private deployment, audit logs can be kept in your KMS-backed S3; Redwood's control plane logs are configurable — we can provide the enrollment doc.

[13:30] Amira: Another functional point — we saw a reranking regression when fallback triggers; response quality drops by 4-6% on our eval suite. Can we control which model variant runs on fallback so quality is preserved?
[13:55] Maya: Yes we support model variants that are quality-equivalent, and also a policy to prefer quality over latency for certain routes. We'll surface the model selection matrix.

[15:20] Daniel: Any visibility into token-level cost impact when we fallback? We need to model the economics for our budget.
[15:33] Luis: Our dashboards show fallback to hosted increases per-token cost ~2.5x compared to reserved local pool; we'll attach cost breakdowns in the follow-up.

[16:10] Ethan: Ok recap on technical mitigations: 1) hold kernel upgrade until we add extra health checks; 2) add routing pin to avoid partial-mixed state during rollback; 3) run MTU/egress tests; 4) confirm encryption & log retention on fallback.

[18:00] Tom: Quick question on routing pin. Is that enforced in the agent or at the VPC peering layer? We need to understand whether it requires config changes on our side.
[18:20] Maya: It's at our router layer - the Redwood edge will honor a session affinity token, we emit that via the SDK. Minimal changes on your side: accept sticky session header or configure LB to preserve source IP. We'll send examples.

[20:05] Amira: For acceptance criteria — besides the p95 < 220ms, we want 99th percentile < 600ms during peak; no data exfiltration events; and a documented runbook for canary rollback. Are we aligned?
[20:30] Ethan: Yep that's alignable. We'll codify acceptance checklist and drop in the shared folder.

[22:10] Sofia: On the SOC2 ask — we need an explicit statement about data residency in the hosted fallback and whether customer can opt out entirely.
[22:30] Ethan: Customers can opt out of hosted fallback; there's a config flag to disallow fallback and instead queue with a degraded SLA. We'll document tradeoffs.

[24:00] Luis: We also recommend a small cache-warmup phase after deployment: pre-warm common prefixes to avoid first-request latency spikes. For your workload the hotspot prefixes were user prompt templates.
[24:30] Amira: That could help — do you provide warmup tooling?
[24:40] Maya: We have a warmup runner that can replay synthetic traffic from a controlled pool. We'll provide a script and a suggested set of prefixes.

[26:10] Daniel: On monitoring, can we get token-level tracing to our Splunk? We need to ingest span markers.
[26:25] Luis: Yes, we can forward traces with sampling rules; we'll coordinate data schema. Note: we scrub PII by default unless flagged.

[28:00] Tom: Re: MTU — we ran traceroute and saw fragmentation between our colo and the cloud egress; we can patch MTU on our router but wanted Redwood's opinion on jumbo frames or path MTU discovery tweaks.
[28:25] Maya: Jumbo frames could help, but path MTU discovery plus consistent MSS clamp is safer. We'll share our ops note on recommended settings.

[30:15] Amira: One last question on encryption keys: if fallback uses Redwood's KMS, can we bring our own key (BYOK)?
[30:27] Ethan: Yes BYOK is supported in private deployment; for hosted fallback there's a limited BYOK pattern but we recommend keeping their key in your cloud KMS and configuring the control plane to use it. We'll add exact steps.

[32:00] Sofia: We'll need to run this past legal for data flow diagrams. Can Redwood produce a simple egress diagram showing where data moves during fallback vs. normal?
[32:12] Hannah: Absolutely, we'll produce a diagram and a one-page data flow description.

[33:30] Maya: Back to the kernel patch — propose we do the following timeline: 1) revert to previous kernel immediately for prod pools, 2) run two smoke canaries with the enhanced checks in staging, 3) re-run a weighted canary across 5% traffic for 90 minutes, 4) soak test 24h in a non-critical region.
[34:00] Tom: Fine with that. Can you also add stepped quantization toggles? We saw slightly different latency shapes on quantized models.
[34:20] Maya: We'll include quantization profiles per model and recommend the one for your workload.

[36:00] Amira: For the POC acceptance sign-off, what's the final artifact we need? A checklist? A runbook? Benchmarks?
[36:12] Ethan: All of the above. We'll deliver a single package: acceptance checklist, the runbook (with rollback steps and playbooks), benchmark spreadsheets (p50/p95/p99) and the compliance evidence pointers.

[38:05] Daniel: Any blockers on our side to finish these tests this week? We need to sync on calendar times for canaries.
[38:18] Ethan: How about two canary windows: Friday 12/18 02:00-04:00 PT and Monday 12/21 06:00-07:30 PT?
[38:30] Amira: Friday works for us. We'll confirm Monday after internal scheduling.

[40:00] Sofia: I'll pull the SOC2 contact and check whether we need an NDA extension for auditor access — may have to route that through legal.

[41:10] Maya: Quick note on observability: we'll push a dashboard template to the folder that includes fallback counts, per-node kernel uptime, KV hit rate, and tail-latency heatmap.
[41:30] Luis: And we'll add automated alerts for >3% fallback rate in a 5-minute window or p95 >220ms.

[42:45] Ethan: Great. Let's quickly recap next steps — I'll read them out. Ethan to share kernel rollback playbook and canary test plan by 12/17, Maya to send routing pin examples and warmup script by 12/18, Luis to publish alerting thresholds and cost breakdown, Sofia to share SOC2/ISO contact by 12/20, Tom to upload pcap/traceroute. BlueHarbor to confirm Friday canary.

[44:05] Amira: Sounds good. One last ask — can you include a short section in the runbook about how to disable fallback entirely and what the expected behavior will be? We want to show that to legal.
[44:20] Ethan: Yep we'll include that with tradeoffs.

[45:00] Ethan: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up in the shared drive and set up the deep-dive. Meeting adjourned.

End of transcript.
